transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... it's about work. Dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes. They do it through the computer system, and I keep hearing these little comments on the radio about it. People keep trying to tell me it’s just normal oversight, you know, just part of the job, but... I can tell certain drivers are definitely reporting on me.
Have you been using any stimulant drugs, like amphetamines, cocaine, or excessive caffeine/energy drinks, or any other recreational substances recently?

No, I don't use any of that. I mean, I drink a cup of coffee before my shift starts, but just a normal amount. I don't drink those energy drinks or take any... recreational drugs. Definitely no cocaine or amphetamines or anything like that. Just regular coffee.

Over the past few weeks, have you noticed any periods where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or energetic, or on the other hand, periods where you felt very down, hopeless, or lost interest in things?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't feel unusually high or energetic... and I'm not depressed or hopeless either. I mean, I'm definitely stressed out about what's happening at work with the tracking and the radio, but my mood itself is just normal. I haven't had any extreme ups or downs.
How long have you been noticing these comments on the radio and feeling that certain drivers are reporting on you—has this been going on for weeks, or longer than six months?

It hasn't been six months, no. I'd say... it's been about two months. The tracking through the computer system and the comments I hear on the radio, it's all felt very clear to me for about the past two months.
Besides hearing comments about you on the radio, have you noticed any other unusual experiences—like seeing things others don't see, or finding it hard to organize your thoughts or speech?

I haven't seen anything that isn't there, no. And my thoughts feel fine to me, but I guess... well, I do have this thing I've been doing at work lately. 

Sometimes I'll get stuck rearranging the magnets and the route slips into a certain pattern on the dispatch board. And when a driver calls in, I end up repeating their last few words back to them before I actually answer. People look at me like I'm just being difficult on purpose, but I'm not. I'm really just doing it to keep the whole board from going wrong.
Over these past two months, has your work performance or your relationships with coworkers and family changed noticeably because of these experiences?

Yes, things have definitely changed. At work, I've fallen behind on my route reports. And my instructions over the radio have gotten confusing enough lately that the drivers are actually complaining about me. It's just... hard to manage it all right now with everything going on. 

And at home, I'm just not keeping up. My husband has had to step in and take over pretty much everything. He's doing the meals, handling phone calls, and doing all the basic planning for the house because I'm just not able to keep up with it all.

I don't know if my face looks different to people, but my motivation is definitely gone. I just don't have the desire to do things I used to enjoy. I don't feel like singing with my choir anymore, or having the softball team over to the house. 

And like I was saying about things at home... most days after my shift, I just sit at the kitchen table. I'll have the planner open right in front of me, but I just can't make myself actually start dinner, or make any phone calls, or do anything else. I just sit there.

Before you started noticing the radio comments and tracking two months ago, did you notice any earlier changes—like withdrawing from friends, losing motivation, or feeling 'off' compared to your usual self—that started earlier, maybe four to six months ago?

Actually, it started a bit earlier than that. I think... well, this has been building for about eight months now. It really started right around the time they put me in the temporary dispatch lead role at work. That's when I first started noticing things changing.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports persecutory delusions (belief that coworkers are reporting on her) and auditory hallucinations of a referential nature (hearing comments about her on the radio) persisting for 2 months, with disorganized/catatonic-like behaviors (repetitive echolalia, ritualistic ordering of dispatch materials), and prominent negative symptoms (anhedonia, avolition, social withdrawal from choir and softball). Total symptom duration is approximately 8 months when including prodromal decline in functioning, satisfying the 6-month criterion. Clear functional impairment is present at work (falling behind on reports, confusing radio instructions) and at home (husband assuming household responsibilities). No manic or depressive episodes were identified, ruling out mood disorder with psychotic features or schizoaffective disorder. No substance use (stimulants, excessive caffeine, or other drugs) accounts for the symptoms, ruling out substance-induced psychosis. The combination of positive, negative, and disorganized symptoms with functional decline over more than 6 months supports a diagnosis of Schizophrenia, unspecified (F20.9).
